newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Mexico markets respond with election joy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mexico markets respond with election joy.

text.p: Mexico's financial markets reacted with joy on Monday to the smooth mid-term elections on Sunday, with interest rates dropping and the peso and stock market strengthening sharply.
Economists said investors will now start to focus on Mexico's improving fundamentals.

"I believe the market will focus on the fact that the eocnomic fundamentals are steadily improving and this will drive the Mexican market over the next 18 months," Morgan Stanley Dean Witter economist Jay Pelosky said in a report.

Results for Sunday's elections showed the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its 68-year grip on the Chamber of Deputies. It was also beaten in the first race for Mexico City mayor this century by left-wing populist Cuauhtemoc Cardenas.
-- The Mexican peso trimmed some of its initial sharp gains by late morning trade on Monday but was still strong on a warm market reception to a smooth mid-term electoral process on Sunday.
The benchmark 48-hour peso was 2.7 centavos firmer at 7.9165/7.920 per dollar.
-- Mexican stocks sharply extended their initial gains to a new intraday record in early trade on Monday.

Dealers said stocks were in heavy demand due to investor relief that Sunday's mid-term elections had taken place in relative calm despite the ruling party suffering its worst setback since 1929. The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 1.26 percent, at 4,703.14.
"Traders also report client flows in Mexican markets remain strong and players remain very bullish on Mexican equities and fixed income paper," MMS International said in a report.
-- Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened down sharply but then gave up some of those gains to traded down 180 basis points at 18.85 percent.
"The market is in a great mood above all because the elections had been exerting upside pressure on rates," a fixed-income analyst said.
